advance_rationale: Fresh pass-2 evidence clears the single carried concern, and an independent residual sweep of head/shoulders, torso/pelvis, prop and whole view finds no remaining axis-level mismatch. The axes clarify the P1 pose without replacing it and no P3 volume vocabulary has leaked in, so primary masses can now be built.
carried_concerns: shoulder axis sits ~13px above the observed far shoulder joint
contract_findings: The correction changed one axis endpoint pair only; the stage still holds axes exclusively and nothing from P3 volume vocabulary has entered.
corrections: P2B-R1 lowered the shoulder axis onto the observed joint line.
drawing_findings: Carried concern 'shoulder axis ~13px high' is CLEARED: the head_shoulders crop now shows the axis running at deltoid-joint level, clearly distinct from the arcing P1 shoulder rhythm rather than doubling it.
torso_pelvis residual sweep: shoulder and pelvis axes counter-tilt and explain the same pose P1 established; neither reads as an unrelated horizontal bar.
prop_overlap residual sweep: extent axis plus two short breadth axes state the rifle's direction and width changes without becoming a contour or a closed mass.
Whole-view residual sweep: both arm chains, both leg chains and the head cross-axis remain correct, the P1 gesture is still the dominant mark, and support versus counterbalance is still unambiguous.
No new axis-level mismatch was found.
exemplar_findings: The audited PASS P2 exemplar's line hierarchy was matched: the axes stay lighter than the inherited P1 gesture.
observations: The correction changed one axis endpoint pair only; the stage still holds axes exclusively and nothing from P3 volume vocabulary has entered.
Re-measured shoulder joints confirm a shallow drop toward the near image-right shoulder; the corrected axis reproduces it.
Shoulder axis and pelvis axis run in opposite senses on the subject, which is what carries the mild torso twist of the back-three-quarter turn.
The rifle's two widest points on the subject, the scope/receiver and the skeleton buttstock, sit where the two breadth axes were placed.
